subject: Pharmacology
concept: Antimalarial medicines are selected according to parasite species, severity, resistance pattern and patient factors.

content.definition: Medicines used to prevent or treat malaria.
content.explanation: Major teaching groups include artemisinin-based combinations, quinoline-related agents and drugs active against liver-stage parasites.
content.mechanism: Different classes act at different parasite stages and biological targets.
high_yield: ACT is a central treatment approach for uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
Severe malaria requires prompt parenteral antimalarial therapy.
Primaquine and tafenoquine have important liver-stage activity and require attention to G6PD status.

review_notes: Educational synthesis aligned with current WHO malaria guidance.
